title: Gluing supported cohomology in its lowest local degree
statement:
Use finite coefficients and supported cohomology [def-pur-conventions], [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed, let $a\in\mathbf Z$, and let $d\geq0$. On the small etale site write $C=R\underline\Gamma_Z(A(a))$ for the derived sheaf of sections with support (the right-derived kernel of restriction to the open complement), and $\mathcal H_Z^q(A(a))=\mathcal H^q(C)$. Suppose $\mathcal H_Z^q(A(a))=0$ for all $q<d$. Then the canonical edge isomorphisms
$$H^d_{Z\times_XU}(U_{\mathrm{et}},A(a))\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(U,\mathcal H_Z^d(A(a))|_U)$$
hold for every etale $U\to X$ and commute with further etale restriction. Under the canonical etale-to-pro-etale supported-cohomology comparison, they identify the pro-etale supported groups with the same sections. Consequently degree-$d$ supported classes have unique gluing on every Zariski or etale covering of $X$. The vanishing hypothesis is essential; no such gluing assertion is made in degrees above the first possible nonzero local-cohomology degree.
